title: Replace can destroy the existing destination on copy failure
governing_basis: Draft F-011 preservation intent; target Preservation Over Perfection / Reliability and Data Integrity
observation: With an existing synthetic destination and a source that disappeared, .replace removed the destination and returned a failed copy. The old bytes were gone. Removal precedes coordinated staging/publish. The same pre-removal branch serves move.
counter_evidence: Ordinary copy uses private staging, no-follow copying and exclusive publish; its control succeeded.
material_unknowns: Move failure, disk-full, crash and permission-revocation variants were not dynamically exercised.
recommendation: Stage and validate the incoming item before replacing; keep the old item recoverable until publish and record rollback outcome. Do the replacement inside the coordinated transaction.
verification: Repeat disappeared-source, denied-read, disk-full and cancellation scenarios with a pre-existing target; original target must remain recoverable on failed publish.
confidence: Strong for stated observation; qualified by listed material UNKNOWNs
root_cause_status: Established contributing branch: destination removal precedes incoming-item staging and validation.
